items.content_html:
Description of changes

Building a NixOS disk image results in an error when compiled without Nix tooling, as indicated by the use of the option nix.enable = false;. Disabling Nix tools through this option not only deactivates general Nix tools but also deletes NixOS installer tools. Consequently, an error is encountered in the nixos/lib/make-disk-image.nix file due to the absence of the nixos-install component.

To address this issue, it is worth noting the availability of the system.disableInstallerTools option, which serves the purpose of disabling installer tools specifically. Therefore, adjusting the configuration by using nix.enable = false; should not interfere with the presence of NixOS installation tools, as this can be managed separately through system.disableInstallerTools.

Component:

nixos/installer/tools: remove nix tooling dependency from nixos config

items.content_html:
Description of changes

With 23.11, nixos-containers won't build unless the option nixpkgs.hostPlatform is set.

Here's a minimal reproducible example:

{
  description = "nixos-containers bug demo";

  inputs.nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/23.11";

  outputs = { self, nixpkgs }: {
    nixosModules.default = { pkgs, modulesPath, ... }: {
      containers.foo.config = {
        environment.systemPackages = [ pkgs.hello ];
        system.stateVersion = "22.05";
      };
      system.stateVersion = "22.05";
    };

    nixosConfigurations = {
      broken = nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem rec {
        pkgs = nixpkgs.legacyPackages.x86_64-linux;
        modules = [
          "${nixpkgs}/nixos/modules/virtualisation/qemu-vm.nix"
          self.nixosModules.default
        ];
      };
    };
  };
}

This results in the following error:

❯ nix flake check
error: Neither nixpkgs.hostPlatform nor the legacy option nixpkgs.system has been set.
       You can set nixpkgs.hostPlatform in hardware-configuration.nix by re-running
       a recent version of nixos-generate-config.
       The option nixpkgs.system is still fully supported for NixOS 22.05 interoperability,
       but will be deprecated in the future, so we recommend to set nixpkgs.hostPlatform.

This PR fixes the problem by using pkgs.stdenv instead of nixpkgs.system.

items.content_html:
This provides the needed infrastructure to make tooling like ofborg build the relevant tests, given a set of changed files.

Having mandatory CI for modules is not just crucial for DX, but also prerequisite to test-driven expansion of NixOS use cases, such as alternate base module sets. (minimal module list and similar ideas)

The option is documented.
We can provide additional instructional docs elsewhere when this is wired into ofborg.

Why not infer the mapping automatically?

Basically the same reasons we have passthru.tests.nixos.

  1. Too costly. We'd have to evaluate all tests to figure out which ones changed.
  2. For some modules it is not feasible to run all affected tests, because that set is too large. We need a representative smaller set.
  3. This could perhaps be scripted as a one-off or infrequent process that updates the mapping, but then it is time of all evals * *number of files under nixos/... And then there's still some risk that it's not a good mapping for some reason. Doesn't solve (2)

items.content_html:
Introduce a new NixOS module networking.gaiConf to allow declarative configuration of /etc/gai.conf, which controls address selection behavior for getaddrinfo(3) as defined in RFC 3484 and RFC 6724.

TODO:

  • add a nixosTest for this module

Background

The GNU C Library (glibc) uses /etc/gai.conf to override default address sorting preferences when resolving hostnames. These preferences are crucial in dual-stack environments (IPv4 + IPv6), where connection choices can affect latency, reachability, and policy compliance.

Per the gai.conf(5) and RFC 3484 §2.1, the address selection process considers:

  • Precedence values (to prefer e.g. native IPv6 over 6to4),
  • Scope and label rules (for local site routing preferences),
  • And optional runtime reloading (reload directive).

Implement

This module:

  • Is enabled by default on glibc systems.
  • Exposes three customizable tables: label, precedence, and scopev4.
  • Skips generation if all tables are null (thus deferring to glibc's defaults).

References

  • RFC 3484: Default Address Selection for Internet Protocol Version 6 (IPv6)
    https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3484
  • RFC 6724: Updated Default Address Selection for IPv6
    https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6724
  • man 5 gai.conf: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man5/gai.conf.5.html
  • man 3 getaddrinfo: https://man7.org/linux/man-pages/man3/getaddrinfo.3.html

items.content_html:
efingerd is another finger daemon, giving you complete control over what are you going to display about your computer. It's similar to bsd-fingerd, however efingerd allows the user complete control over what to send via .efingerd executable in their home directory. efingerd also has the ability to use the ident protocol to allow the user to configure a different responses per the querier's username and host.
